text: Excellent service, and the doctor did a beautiful job.

It's difficult to share my experience as a guide and encouragement for doctors. The picture is from breast augmentation done 10 days ago by Dr. Kob Naruephon. I decided to have it done here because a clinic I used recommended him. We consulted, agreed on the price, and decided to use Motiva Ekinmonic silicone with an embedded chip, the top model at the clinic, because I liked how soft and natural the silicone was. Personally, I wanted my breast augmentation to look natural. On the day of the surgery, I arrived as scheduled at 9:00 AM. The doctor gave me one pill to relax me (I heard some places require nine pills!). The surgery was at 10:00 AM. I have to say, the anesthesiologist was very skilled and professional. I think other women should also be aware of this. With over 20 years of experience, the doctor explained what to expect, talking to me and gently stroking my arm to keep me calm. Importantly, this clinic uses a scarless technique – no stitches, just grafts. You can get it wet immediately; no need to wait weeks. I woke up looking great. I don't know if others experienced this, but I woke up without dizziness or pain. I thought, "Okay, day two is going to be tough." Day two arrived, though slightly painful because I was wearing a tight bra and couldn't lie flat properly (initially I had to lie with my head elevated at 45 degrees). I took one pill and it was fine. Day three was very relaxed; I didn't need anyone to help me get up, sit up, or shower because there was no pain, just some stiffness. On day three, I went to the beach. On day 4, I ate out. On day 5, I drove because I didn't feel any pain at all. I didn't see the point in staying home. On day 6, I went to work and drove comfortably. The doctor wasn't worried at all about this case. The doctor said I could start exercising in a week, like walking or cycling. Weightlifting should wait 3-4 weeks.

Things to avoid: alcohol, beer, cigarettes, and fermented/pickled foods. (I drink alcohol, but don't try this yourself! Everyone's body is different. I didn't experience any pain.) I'll end it here for now. "Being run over by a truck" is a myth. Implantable contraception is much more painful, I'm telling you!
